summary: First-iteration full-stack testing of KHALABA MVP. Created 21 pytest backend tests covering auth/OTP, zones, structures, patients, pregnancies, CPN (with alerts), postnatal (with alerts), children, vaccinations, MPDSR, admin analytics, register, logout. After fixing a CRITICAL backend bug where all POST endpoints returned 500 due to MongoDB ObjectId in response, all 21 backend tests pass. Frontend: landing page renders with KHALABA branding & French copy; 2-step OTP login flow works for admin/soignant/patient and role-based redirect is correct; admin dashboard renders KPIs + BarChart + PieChart (3 Recharts SVGs); soignant patient list + patient detail + open-pregnancy (window.prompt date) + CPN form all working end-to-end; logout clears cookies and returns to /.

issues: Recharts logs width(-1)/height(-1) warnings during first paint; charts render correctly afterwards. Consider giving ResponsiveContainer an explicit minHeight to avoid the console warning.
Uses native browser date input (<input type=date>) rather than a styled shadcn calendar — acceptable for MVP, but inconsistent with the rest of the design system.

action_items: (FIXED by testing agent) Backend POST endpoints were returning 500 because motor.insert_one mutates the doc to add ObjectId _id, which then fails JSON serialization. Patched /app/backend/server.py to pop _id after every insert_one(doc) and to exclude _id from the register endpoint's public payload. Please verify the patch matches your style preferences (alternative: use a wrapper helper, or pass a copy to insert_one).
Consider giving Recharts ResponsiveContainer an explicit min-height in AdminDashboard.jsx to silence width/height(-1) warnings on first paint.
MPDSR model requires place_of_death and medical_cause (not 'location'/'cause_probable'). Frontend MPDSRPage.jsx should be cross-checked to ensure it submits the correct field names.
critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL FIXED: All POST endpoints (zones, structures, patients, pregnancies, cpn-visits, postnatal-visits, children, vaccinations, mpdsr, appointments, register) returned 500 because they returned the doc after insert_one — and motor mutates the dict to add the bson ObjectId _id, which FastAPI cannot serialize. Pattern fix applied: doc.pop('_id', None) after each insert_one(doc).
OTP code is returned in the API response (intentional demo mode per problem statement) — fine for MVP but must be removed before production.

CORS configured with allow_origins=['*'] AND allow_credentials=True — browsers will reject Set-Cookie with wildcard origin. The allow_origin_regex='.*' also yields '*' in some setups. For production, set an explicit origin list.
Auth analytics endpoint does N+1 queries (per zone, per pregnancy) — fine for low cardinality but should be replaced with an aggregation pipeline at scale.
server.py is 627 lines — recommend splitting routes into modules (auth, patients, pregnancies, analytics) before it grows.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the 500s: motor's AsyncIOMotorCollection.insert_one mutates the input dict in-place by injecting a BSON ObjectId under the '_id' key. The route handlers then returned that same dict, and FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize bson.ObjectId, raising ValueError. Mitigation: after each insert_one(doc), call doc.pop('_id', None) (or pass doc.copy() to insert_one). Applied across all 10 POST endpoints in server.py and the register endpoint's response builder. Verified by re-running the pytest suite — all 21 tests now pass.
